features.name: 100% code coverage testing pattern
features.description: A coding pattern using interfaces to achieve 100% code coverage in AL objects, enabling fast tests that cover all code paths in tested objects.
caveats: Only covers 100% of code in objects being tested, not all objects

features.name: Payment API integration with environment-aware mode switching
features.description: Integration with online payment provider that automatically switches to test mode in non-production environments and test mode in sandbox, preventing production API calls during development.

features.name: Fast automated testing framework
features.description: Tests run in milliseconds with over 200 test cases, enabling developers to run tests continuously as part of development workflow.

features.name: GitHub AL-Go integration with test reporting
features.description: CI-CD pipeline using AL-Go for GitHub showing test results and status checks for payment integration app with multiple test apps.

features.name: Context interfaces pattern
features.description: A design pattern using enums to define different implementation contexts. Instead of using event subscribers scattered throughout standard code, extensions can implement their own versions of interfaces through enum extensions, enabling customization without modifying core code.

features.name: Environment interfaces
features.description: Interfaces that abstract the execution environment including the underlying platform (sandbox vs production), current company, and evaluation company status. These interfaces enable testing different environment scenarios and achieving full code coverage.
caveats: requires careful code organization and splitting functions into smaller units

features.name: Enum-based state management
features.description: Using enums instead of booleans to represent application states, reducing cyclomatic complexity and making impossible states impossible. Helps prevent illegal state combinations that could introduce bugs.

features.name: Test doubles with stubs and spies
features.description: Using stub objects that return fixed data without tracking usage, and spy objects that record function calls for verification. These testing techniques allow controlling and monitoring system behavior during tests.

features.name: Environment stub implementation for testing
features.description: Using stub implementations of system environment interfaces to control environment behavior during testing, allowing tests to simulate production or sandbox environments without actual environment changes.
caveats: Must use temporary records in tests
Requires setting up stub objects before testing logic

features.name: API testing without external calls
features.description: Testing API functionality by creating interface implementations that simulate HTTP responses without making actual external calls, allowing tests to verify handling of success and failure scenarios.
caveats: Does not test the actual HTTP client implementation
Requires creating interface implementations for API methods

features.name: API spy variables for tracking calls
features.description: Using global spy variables in test codeunits to track which API functions were called and verify that logic around API calls handles success and failure scenarios correctly.
caveats: Test code can become complex with many spy variables

features.name: Record parameter passing for fast testing
features.description: Passing record variables by reference through function parameters instead of retrieving them from the database allows testing function logic with temporary records, eliminating database operations and making tests fast.
caveats: Requires refactoring existing functions to accept record parameters

features.name: Application state management for test scenarios
features.description: Using application state variables to distinguish between production and test modes, allowing email and phone number substitution from setup records during testing to prevent sending real communications.
caveats: Not using interfaces for this pattern

features.name: Single database get optimization
features.description: By passing setup records at the top level and passing them down through multiple functions, developers can reduce multiple database gets to a single get operation.

features.name: AI assistance for code generation and testing
features.description: Using AI tools like Claude to write functions and automatically generate and run tests based on existing code patterns, with AI being particularly effective when code follows consistent patterns.

features.name: Event publishers for separating concerns
features.description: Using event publishers and subscribers to decouple side effects from pure business logic, keeping the core functions clean while handling side effects like writing to event tables separately.

features.name: Pure functions for testability
features.description: Writing pure functions that have no side effects and do not perform database operations directly, making them easier to test and allowing AI to generate and run tests automatically.
caveats: True pure functions are difficult in AL due to database requirement

features.name: Dependency injection parameter hell trade-off
features.description: Moving setup retrieval to parameters follows dependency injection principles but can lead to excessive parameters if not designed carefully, requiring developers to rethink design or introduce interfaces.
caveats: Risk of accumulating too many parameters at top level

features.name: Modular app architecture
features.description: Approach to organize code into multiple apps, which increases complexity in terms of dependencies but reduces the context the AI has to look at, helping avoid parameter hell scenarios.
caveats: trade-offs between single vs multiple apps

features.name: API operation record pattern
features.description: Pattern of putting all information needed for an API call into a record, allowing a single function to handle any API call without needing many parameters, including endpoint, request method, payload, and response.
caveats: complexity is moved into the record structure

features.name: Interface pattern for consistent signatures
features.description: Use of interfaces to ensure that functions have similar parameter signatures, making it easier to manage complexity and maintain code consistency.
